# TRK-1 plan: Pod policy profiles (impl-xlarge@1, step plan, Run run_89963994885a)

Base: `origin/main` 07093ab, rechecked 2026-11-08 in this Run; the ticket was proved on 96d2999 and every Constraint still holds. Branch: `trk-dev/tpc-1413-pod-policy-profiles` (clean, at 07093ab).

Provenance: this is the plan the coordinator pair agreed in Run run_4fa85deae9c8 (Decision dec_cbbf711d, accept_plan, round 1, auditor agree, D1 included; posted on TRK-1 by the lead). The base has not moved since then and no implementation landed, so the plan carries over unchanged. The one change is section "Forward compatibility with S16b", added because TRK-15 (S16b) was filed after that Decision and names this ticket's pending path.

## What the code does today (07093ab, each line rechecked)

- `specs/policy/default.yaml` `profiles` defines only `autonomous` (`replaces` both liftable Gates). No profile has a `deploy_production` key.
- `src/core/config/policy.ts`: `profileProblem` (line 85) checks only `replaces`. `activeProfile` (line 261) reads `active_profile`. Nothing checks that `active_profile` names a defined profile.
- `src/core/config/apply.ts` `policyRefusal` (lines 150-160) refuses every `active_profile` with `gate_lift_refused`, using `tx.liveRunsPinningPolicyScope`.
- `pod config apply --activate --scope --expected-revision` already exists (`src/cli/config-verbs.ts`). Activation is immediate: one transaction inserts the operation, the Revision, the `config.activation` row, and an `activation` event, then moves the operation to `done`. `ledger.operation.status` already allows `pending`.
- `pod run create` (`src/core/run/create.ts:255-258`) resolves crew and policy at **global scope only**. A Run records no project. `config.snapshot` has no project column and no profile column, and `effective_gate_map` is always `{}`.
- `pod check` is a per-Run pass (`checkPass`, `--run`, fenced by owner generation). S13b reads human rulings in `applyRulings` (`src/core/check/check.ts:250`), which calls `verifiedRulings` (`src/core/gate/ruling.ts:27`): a tracker readback of the Run's Story, then `verifySource` against the pinned policy's HQA keepers and relay principal, the bypass record, the readback hash compare, and the consumed-comment check.
- `pod state --project <ref>` resolves policy at project scope and falls back to global (`src/core/state/view.ts`). `policiesSection` builds the policies section.
- `reservedOf` (`src/core/domain/policy.ts:184`) is called by `src/core/decide/open.ts:204`.
- Migrations end at `0012_prompt_bytes.sql`, so the new one is `0013_*`.
- Tech spec: `#### Gate-lift` says "In v1 the executor refuses every profile activation". Conformance row 8 says "every gate-lift activation is refused". The spec has no TRK-3 section.

## Design decisions the pair must agree

D1. **A Run knows its project.** Q7, Q8, and "the next `pod run create`" all need this, and a Run has no project today. `pod run create` gains an optional `--project <ref>`. With it, crew and policy resolve through `singleActive(db, kind, "project", ref)`, which already falls back to global. Without it, they resolve at global scope as they do today. Migration `0013_*` adds two nullable text columns to `config.snapshot`: `project` and `profile`. Both are written once at pin time and never updated; no repo method updates a snapshot, and none is added. The ticket names only the profile column, so `project` is the one addition beyond the Constraints. Rejected alternative: derive the project from the `scope_ref` of the pinned policy Revision. A Run that pinned the global fallback would then have no project, so Q7's list and Q8's marker would miss it.

D2. **The pending request lives in the operation row; there is no new table.** Take an `--activate` apply whose Revision is a project-scope policy with `active_profile` set to `hands-on`, `standard`, or `hands-off`. The apply stores the Revision, inserts the `config_apply` operation, and leaves the operation `pending` with `result_ref = { pending: { scope, scope_ref, kind, name, revision_id, expected, profile, comment } }`. It writes no `config.activation` row and no `activation` event. The reply carries `activation: null` and a new `pending` object holding the comment text and `runs_on_old_profile`. `pod config apply` never posts anything. Replaying the apply with the same op key returns the same pending result: extend `recorded()` to handle status `pending` with a `pending` result_ref. This needs no migration.

D3. **The comment form binds the Revision.** The comment is one line, `profile <project> <name> <policy ref>`, for example `profile dogfood hands-on policy.default@7`. Optional note lines may follow, and the comment is parsed the way `parseRuling` parses a ruling. Including the ref keeps one comment from activating a later Revision.

D4. **The readback runs inside `pod check --run R`.** After `applyRulings`, a new `applyProfileActivations` matches R's Story comments against the pending operations. It reuses the readback that `verifiedRulings` already makes, so the comments are read once. It verifies the source through the same `verifySource` and readback-hash path. The part that `verifiedRulings` and the refusal path share is factored into one helper in `src/core/gate/ruling.ts`, not copied. Keepers come from the policy **currently active** at the pending scope (project, else global) and never from the pending Revision, so a Revision cannot name its own approver.
- A verified comment runs one transaction. It calls `tx.activate` with the recorded `expected`, appends an `activation` event with `source: { kind: "tracker_comment", comment_id, author, readback_at }`, and moves the operation to `done` with the normal `ApplyResult`.
- On `revision_conflict`, the operation moves to `refused` as it does today, and a next step is pushed.
- An unverified comment pushes `receipt_unverified_source` text to `nextSteps` and leaves the operation pending.
- The person posts the comment on the Story of any Run whose coordinator runs `pod check`, and the apply reply states that rule. An activation path without a Run is out of scope (TRK-8 / S16b).

D5. **Profile validation.** A profile entry accepts only the keys `replaces`, `requires`, and `deploy_production`. `deploy_production` must be `needs_human` or `agent`. `active_profile` must name a key in the same Revision's `profiles`; otherwise the apply fails with `schema_invalid` at path `active_profile`. The liftable set stays `prd_review` and `design_clickthrough`. `droppedMember` is unchanged.

D6. **`autonomous` stays refused.** `policyRefusal` refuses it with `gate_lift_refused`. The message names the profile, and `nextSteps` points at "Gate-lift" in `docs/tech-spec.md`, whose new Spec clarification says autonomous waits on the step method override. No ticket keys appear in `src/` (scope scan).

D7. **The effect of `deploy_production: agent`** is one pure function in `src/core/domain/policy.ts`, beside `reservedOf`. `effectiveReserved(policyValue)` drops the `deploy_production` needs_human member only when the active profile says `agent`, and `src/core/decide/open.ts:204` calls it in place of `reservedOf`. The path is unreachable in practice while autonomous is refused, so a unit test on a constructed value covers it.

D8. **Lifts are not enforced here.** `effective_gate_map` stays `{}`, and Gate keeper resolution is unchanged. `hands-off` lifts matter only to prd and design processes, and TRK-3 owns that table. The Spec clarification says so. If the pair wants the lift recorded in `effective_gate_map`, T2 can add it cheaply, though nothing reads it.

D9. **The Q7 list.** `runs_on_old_profile` uses `liveRunsPinningPolicyScope`, widened to match `snapshot.project = ref` as well as the scope of the pinned Revision. A Run that pinned the global fallback under `--project ref` is then listed.

## Forward compatibility with S16b (TRK-15, filed after the earlier Decision)

S16b is blocked by this ticket. It will move the `active_profile` pending path onto a new `config_activate` operation intent and an `activation_requested` event, using the migration after `0013_*`. It keeps `profile <project> <name>` as a synonym comment, and this ticket's tests stay green. The plan above fits that move with no change:
- The pending request uses the existing `config_apply` intent with status `pending` (D2), so S16b changes that one intent value through its own migration.
- D3's comment starts `profile <project> <name>`, so S16b's synonym rule matches it; the trailing `<policy ref>` is extra binding.
- S16b reads comments on the tickets that hold pending requests. D4 reads the comments on the Run's Story. S16b widens the source, and D4's single shared verify helper is the one it extends.
- S16b adds `agent_activates: []` to all four profiles. D5's closed key set (`replaces`, `requires`, `deploy_production`) is the line S16b extends. Keep the key check in one place in `profileProblem`.

## Tasks (one per Checkpoint, run in order: T2 needs T1, T3 needs T2)

### T1 Rules
Files: `specs/policy/default.yaml`, `src/core/config/policy.ts`, `src/core/domain/policy.ts`, `src/core/decide/open.ts`, `src/core/config/apply.ts` (only the `active_profile` membership check and the autonomous refusal; the pending path is T2), and the new `test/config/policy-profiles.test.ts` (a new directory; `vitest.config.ts` already includes `test/**/*.test.ts`).
- Define four profiles:
  - `hands-on: { deploy_production: needs_human }`
  - `standard: { deploy_production: needs_human }`
  - `hands-off: { replaces: { prd_review, design_clickthrough → decision-pair-aqa }, deploy_production: needs_human }`
  - `autonomous: { replaces: same, deploy_production: agent }`
  The indentation must give `grep -Ec "^    (hands-on|standard|hands-off|autonomous):"` = 4.
- Implement D5, D6, and D7.
- Until T2 lands, a non-autonomous `active_profile` keeps today's refusal, so main stays consistent at every commit.
- Tests:
  - the four definitions load and validate
  - a lift of `hqa_after_deploy` or `staging_review` is refused
  - a bad `deploy_production` value is refused
  - an unknown profile key is refused
  - an `active_profile` that names an undefined profile is refused
  - autonomous activation returns `gate_lift_refused` with the Gate-lift next step
  - `effectiveReserved` keeps `deploy_production` for needs_human and drops it for agent
  - `droppedMember` still refuses dropping a global member
  - `test/replay/gate-lift-refused.test.ts` stays green
Check: the Checkpoint 1 commands.

### T2 Activation
Files:
- `src/core/config/apply.ts`
- `src/cli/config-verbs.ts` (prints the comment and the run list)
- `src/db/schema/config.ts`
- `db/migrations/0013_*.sql`, generated with `drizzle-kit generate` (ADR 0001; never hand-written)
- `src/core/domain/config.ts` (the Snapshot type)
- `src/adapters/postgres/repository.ts` and `src/core/ports/db.ts`: `listPendingProfileOps()`, the snapshot columns, and the widened `liveRunsPinningPolicyScope`
- `src/core/run/create.ts` and `src/cli/run-verbs.ts` (`--project`)
- `src/core/check/check.ts` and `src/core/gate/ruling.ts`
- `test/db/config-apply.test.ts`, plus any fake or fixture Repo that implements the port

Work:
- Implement D1, D2, D3, D4, and D9. Snapshot `profile` = `activeProfile(policy.value)` of the pinned policy. Snapshot `project` = the `--project` value, or null.
- The pair decides whether the two new columns join `snapshotHash`. Recommendation: no. The hash stays over Revision ids, and those already determine the profile.
- Rewrite the test "active_profile is gate_lift_refused, naming a Run with unsettled Tasks" (line ~927) into the pending path.
- Add two cases by exact name:
  - "hands-on activation waits for the human readback": the apply returns pending and writes no activation row. A comment written by a worker leaves the request pending with `receipt_unverified_source`. The keeper's comment activates it on `pod check`. A second check is a no-op.
  - "a Run snapshot keeps its profile after a later activation": a Run created under an active `hands-on` records `profile` and `policy_revision_id`, and a later `standard` activation changes neither.
- Also cover: a switch while a Run is live is accepted and the reply lists that Run, and replaying a pending apply is idempotent.
- `test/db/snapshot-pinned.test.ts`, `run-create*.test.ts`, and `migrate.test.ts` must stay green.
- T3 owns the `docs/contract.md` text. T2 touches the contract only if the contract test fails without it.
Check: the Checkpoint 2 commands, plus `pnpm -s vitest run test/db`.

### T3 Surfaces and proof
Files: `src/core/state/sections.ts`, `src/core/state/render.ts`, `src/core/brief/*`, `src/cli/brief.ts`, `docs/contract.md`, `docs/tech-spec.md`, `package.json`, the new `test/replay/profiles.test.ts`, and `test/replay/profiles/` fixtures shaped like the other replays.
- `pod state`, policies section:
  - `Profile: <name> (policy <rev>)`
  - `Profile: none (policy <rev>)` when no profile is set
  - one `Profile pending: <name> (policy <rev>), post "<comment>"` line for each pending operation at that scope
  - the JSON section gains `profile` and `pending_profile`, beside the existing `source_revision` and `observed_at`
- `pod brief`:
  - one line per project: the distinct `snapshot.project` values and the project-scope policy activations, plus global
  - JSON `profile` per project
  - each Run row gets `profile` from its snapshot, and `profile_stale: true` when that differs from its project's current profile
- Replays, one per activatable profile (hands-on, standard, hands-off): apply pending, post the keeper comment, run `pod check`, then assert the brief JSON `profile` and the state `Profile:` line.
- Tech spec:
  - Add one `Spec clarification:` paragraph under "#### Gate-lift". It covers: a request is pending until the human readback through `pod check`; the comment form; keepers come from the current policy; autonomous is still refused pending the step method override; the snapshot pins the project and the profile; lifts are not enforced in v1.
  - Reword "In v1 the executor refuses every profile activation" to match.
  - Reword row 8 to "every autonomous activation and every lift outside `prd_review` and `design_clickthrough` is refused".
- `docs/contract.md`: the `pod config apply` pending reply, `pod run create --project`, the `pod state` Profile lines, and the `pod brief` `profile` and `profile_stale` fields. The contract test must pass.
- `package.json`: 0.1.0 → 0.1.1.
Check: the Checkpoint 3 commands, then the final-head checks: `pnpm -s vitest run`, the scope scan, `pnpm -s typecheck`, and `pnpm -s lint` (eslint plus depcruise).

## Review and PR

- Each Task gets a `review` from an independent reviewer Seat, then `integration_review` runs on the candidate SHA.
- The PR body pairs each Completion check item with its result (the `pr` skill). It names D1 (the `project` column) as the one addition beyond the Constraints and says the S16b handover in "Forward compatibility" is intended.
- The merge waits on the crew PR review PASS and keeper's HQA PR review PASS. `hqa_after_deploy` follows Q11, using `--project` on later Runs and the comment form in D3.

## Risks

- D1 widens `pod run create`. The S14b Run was created without `--project`, so its snapshot `project` is null. Q11 still works: the keeper applies the Revision to the dogfood project and posts the comment on S14b's Story, `pod check --run <S14b>` activates it, and `pod state --project dogfood` shows the line.
- Because the readback runs per Run, a pending activation waits until some coordinator runs `pod check`. The apply reply and the Spec clarification state this. S16b removes the limit.
- Overlap: TRK-2 also names `docs/tech-spec.md`, and TRK-2 names `package.json`. TRK-13 (#38) is already in the base. Rebase on `origin/main` before T3.

## Design decisions the pair must agree

D1. **A Run knows its project.** Q7, Q8, and "the next `pod run create`" need it, and today a Run has none. `pod run create` gains an optional `--project <ref>`. With it, crew and policy resolve through `singleActive(db, kind, "project", ref)` (which already falls back to global); without it, global as today. Migration `0013_*` adds two nullable text columns to `config.snapshot`: `project` and `profile`. Both are written once at pin time and never updated (no repo method updates a snapshot; add none). The ticket names only the profile column, so `project` is the one addition beyond the Constraints. Alternative considered: derive the project from the pinned policy Revision's `scope_ref`. Rejected because a Run that pinned the global fallback loses its project, so Q7's list and Q8's marker miss it.

D2. **Pending lives in the operation row, not a new table.** An `--activate` apply whose Revision is a policy at project scope with `active_profile` set (`hands-on`, `standard`, `hands-off`) stores the Revision, inserts the `config_apply` operation, and leaves it `pending` with `result_ref = { pending: { scope, scope_ref, kind, name, revision_id, expected, profile, comment } }`. It writes no `config.activation` row and no `activation` event. The reply carries `activation: null` and a new `pending` object with the comment text and `runs_on_old_profile`. `pod config apply` never posts. A replayed apply with the same op key returns the same pending result (extend `recorded()` for status `pending` with a `pending` result_ref). No migration is needed for this.

D3. **Comment form binds the Revision.** `profile <project> <name> <policy ref>`, for example `profile dogfood hands-on policy.default@7`, one line, optional note lines after it, parsed like `parseRuling`. Binding the ref stops one comment from activating a later Revision.

D4. **Readback runs inside `pod check --run R`.** After `applyRulings`, a new `applyProfileActivations` reads R's Story comments once (reuse the readback `verifiedRulings` already makes; do not read twice), matches each comment against the pending operations, and verifies the source with the same `verifySource` + readback-hash path. Factor the shared part of `verifiedRulings`/`refusal` into one helper in `src/core/gate/ruling.ts` rather than copying it. Keepers come from the policy **currently active** at the pending scope (project, else global), never from the pending Revision, so a Revision cannot name its own approver. On a verified comment, one transaction: `tx.activate` with the recorded `expected`, append `activation` event with `source: { kind: "tracker_comment", comment_id, author, readback_at }`, move the operation to `done` with the normal `ApplyResult`. On `revision_conflict`, move it to `refused` as today and push a next step. An unverified comment pushes `receipt_unverified_source` text to `nextSteps` and leaves it pending. The person posts the comment on the Story of any Run whose coordinator runs `pod check`; the apply reply names that rule. A Run-less activation path is out of scope (TRK-8).

D5. **Profile validation.** A profile entry accepts exactly `replaces`, `requires`, `deploy_production`. `deploy_production` must be `needs_human` or `agent`. `active_profile` must name a key of the same Revision's `profiles` (`schema_invalid`, path `active_profile`). Liftable set stays `prd_review`, `design_clickthrough`. `droppedMember` unchanged.

D6. **`autonomous` stays refused** in `policyRefusal` with `gate_lift_refused`, message naming the profile, `nextSteps` pointing at `docs/tech-spec.md` "Gate-lift" (the new Spec clarification says autonomous waits on the step method override). No ticket keys in `src/` (scope scan).

D7. **`deploy_production: agent` effect** is one pure function in `src/core/domain/policy.ts` beside `reservedOf`: `effectiveReserved(policyValue)` drops the `deploy_production` needs_human member only when the active profile says `agent`. `src/core/decide/open.ts:204` calls it instead of `reservedOf`. Unreachable in practice while autonomous is refused; covered by a unit test on a constructed value.

D8. **Lifts are not enforced here.** `effective_gate_map` stays `{}` and Gate keeper resolution is unchanged; `hands-off` lifts only matter to prd/design processes and TRK-3 owns that table. The Spec clarification says so. If the pair wants the lift recorded in `effective_gate_map`, it is a small addition to T2, but nothing reads it.

D9. **Q7 list.** `runs_on_old_profile` = `liveRunsPinningPolicyScope` widened to match `snapshot.project = ref` as well as the pinned Revision scope, so a Run that pinned the global fallback under `--project ref` is listed.
